description: Set who may read a session: private (its authors only), team (every author in your tenant; the default) or link (team, plus anyone authenticated who opens it by exact id; never listed or searched outside the tenant). Only the session's author or an admin token may set it; the latest setting wins and applies to every read at once.

request_key.description: Optional idempotency key; a retry with the same key changes nothing.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

name: set_visibility

description: Request that a session be deleted: from the moment this returns no read (search_sessions, open, list_sessions, file_attention) shows it to anyone. The request is recorded and cannot be undone; the stored data is not physically removed. Only the session's author or an admin token may request it.

request_key.description: Optional idempotency key; defaults to one per session.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

name: delete_session

description: Judge a session or one span of it: append a score (number), a label or a text note, tagged with who or what made the judgment (human, scorer or ci). Annotations are append-only records, never overwritten; the author is your token's, not an argument. Needs a token with the annotate scope and a session you may open. The annotation shows in get_trace after the next converge (a few seconds). A retry with the same request_id, or with the same content when none is given, changes nothing.

label.description: A short categorical value such as pass or regression.

name.description: What is judged, such as correctness or tests_passed.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key; defaults to a hash of the annotation without its time.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

source.description: Who judged: human, scorer (an automatic grader) or ci.

span_id.description: A span id from get_trace; omit to judge the whole session.

name: annotate

description: Return a session's span tree: invoke_agent, turn, chat (model call) and execute_tool spans nested under their parents, with start, end, status, model, token counts and cost where the source reports it, session totals, and the annotations on the session and on each span. The text is the same tree indented one level per depth.

include_annotations.description: Attach the session's annotations; false returns the spans alone.

session_id.description: A session id as list_sessions, search_sessions and open return it (session:...).

name: get_trace

description: Run one read-only SELECT over your tenant's sessions. Name only these views, unqualified: events (one row per event: session_id, event_ts, harness, event_kind, actor_kind, tool_name, tool_call_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, text_content, author, ...), sessions (session_id, first_event_time, last_event_time, total_turns, total_events, tool_calls, user_messages, assistant_messages), turns (session_id, turn_seq, event_count, completed), spans (session_id, span_id, parent_span_id, kind, name, start_time, end_time, status, model, token counts, cost), annotations (annotation_id, target_session_id, target_span_id, name, value_number, value_label, value_text, source, author, ts). Each view holds only rows inside from..to (events by event_ts, spans by start_time, sessions overlapping the range, annotations by ts) and only sessions you may read. from and to are required RFC 3339 timestamps at most 31 days apart. At most limit rows come back (default 100, max 10000; truncated says more existed). A statement runs at most 30 s. Only SELECT, CTEs, joins and an allowlist of scalar, aggregate, window, list, map, struct, date, string, math and json functions are accepted; table functions, file access, other tables and schemas, and multiple statements are refused. When all query slots are busy the server answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

from.description: Start of the range, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp (for example 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z).

sql.description: One SELECT statement over events, sessions, turns, spans and annotations.

to.description: End of the range, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp; at most 31 days after from.

name: query
